key_insight: The paper co-designs the algorithm, error-correcting code, and neutral-atom hardware to make STAR quantum simulation work with high-rate bicycle-chain codes and parallel magic-state injections.
engineering_relevance: It shows a practical path to lower qubit overhead and faster fault-tolerant simulation by exploiting translation symmetry and hardware-native operations.
method: Use translation symmetries of the target lattice to select self-dual bivariate bicycle codes.
Exploit disjoint logical representatives so STAR injections run in parallel across all logical qubits in a block.
Map logical shifts to low-depth acousto-optic-deflector operations on neutral-atom hardware.
evidence_signal: Abstract-level estimates report 2240 physical qubits and about 200 s per shot for 8×8 transverse-field Ising simulation, and about 6300 qubits and 200 s per shot for Fermi-Hubbard dynamics.
watch_item: The results are based on end-to-end estimates and practical performance may still depend on post-selection yield, code overhead, and neutral-atom control fidelity.
paper_title: Fast and Parallel High-Rate STAR Architecture for Megaquop Quantum Simulation
